method: Two local Appendix300 clips sampled every 2 seconds; sequential contact sheets and full-resolution Center1 frames at 12 and 34 seconds inspected. Not a review of the entire dataset.
observed: Curved tubular tissue with nonuniform contours and attached yellow tissue
Lobulated yellow fat interspersed with thin membrane-like sheets and branching vessels
Overlapping bowel folds and layers rather than a few isolated smooth solids
Instrument-associated changes in tissue configuration and exposure across the sequence
Local wet highlights and heterogeneous pink, yellow, pale and red appearance
current_asset_mismatches: Mesoappendix appears as an opaque broad yellow solid; thin sheet and lobulated fat components are not resolved
Large smooth surfaces suppress the layered tissue structure seen in the clips
Appendix-to-cecum registration is heuristic and remains unvalidated
Current rest geometry and render do not establish the tissue connection behaviour visible under manipulation
decision: Rework the surgical-region anatomy and connected tissue layers before further texture-only polishing or claiming baseline visual parity. Keep CT as spatial context; existing atlas is provisional rather than a validated final surgical asset.
next_asset_requirements: Explicit appendix, cecal junction, membrane and fatty tissue components with documented provenance
Separate observed structures from authored geometry; no claim of patient-specific reconstruction from these monocular snippets
Validate both unloaded shape and connected tissue motion during approach, grasp, traction and release
Review additional cases before treating one visible anatomy as representative
limitations: Two convenience-selected clips are not a representative cohort
Exact labels, wall thickness and metric depth cannot be established from these frames alone
The 34-second frame contains strong compression artifacts; exclude those artifacts from surface-detail modelling
No force or calibrated material parameters inferred from video
